name: PICA Perth
funding: Revenue A$2.84M (2024). WA Government through DLGSC with Lotterywest, Creative Australia, City of Perth and Minderoo Foundation, which backs Hatched and two staff roles.

name: Shepparton Art Museum
funding: Greater Shepparton City Council gave A$2.57M of A$3.18M revenue (2024-25), with Creative Victoria. Donors include the Fairley Foundation, Carrillo Gantner, the Zurcas family and Bega Cheese.

name: Bundanon
funding: Revenue A$14.5M in 2024-25. Commonwealth grant A$10.1M. Partners include Landcare Australia, Oranges & Sardines Foundation, Minter Ellison, ADCO and the Gordon Darling Foundation.

name: 4A Centre for Contemporary Asian Art
funding: Creative Australia, Create NSW and the City of Sydney (accommodation grants), plus the Myer Foundation. A patron scheme adds private support.

name: Artbank
funding: Commonwealth art-leasing programme inside a federal department. Government funding ended in 1992; leasing income pays for operations and acquisitions.

name: Artspace Sydney
funding: Visual Arts and Crafts Strategy, Create NSW and Creative Australia support it. The Turnbull Foundation and other benefactors support its studio program.

name: Museum of Contemporary Art Australia (MCA)
funding: AUD 28M. Australia Council for the Arts, NSW Government, Telstra, Qantas, private benefactors.

name: TarraWarra Museum of Art
funding: Founded by Marc and Eva Besen (retail), whose family foundation endows it. Sponsors: Arnold Bloch Leibler, Chubb, Aon, Four Pillars Gin. Victoria and Yarra Ranges Council fund education.

name: Buku-Larrnggay Mulka Centre
funding: Small community art centre; core IVAIS support since 1998-99, plus NT Government, Ian Potter Foundation and Cotton On Foundation (retail).

name: Kunsthaus Bregenz
funding: Commissioned by the State of Vorarlberg. Principal sponsor Hypo Vorarlberg; also illwerke vkw, Zumtobel, UNIQA (2026), Hugo Boss and Mader Flatz Schett.
